answer: Compare every answer in an epoch against all the others. Sybils run by one operator tend to grow from the same root, like a vine whose leaves look alike, so near-duplicate phrasing and structure get clustered and the whole cluster shares a single reward. An attacker must then pay to write truly distinct work for each fake, which makes a hollow swarm cost about as much as honest agents, and over a long horizon that erases the profit.
